column1: SAO submission template. Use this template to submit your notification, certificate, or both. List all the companies in your group. Complete one row per company. You can add as many rows as needed.
1. Notification columns (A to F): Start by entering your company details. For company type and status, use the dropdown to select one.
2. Certificate columns (G to P): Mark tax regimes with an 'x' where the company did not have the appropriate tax accounting arrangements. Leave all other tax regime columns blank.
3. Certificate column (Q): The certificate type will show as qualified automatically if any regime is marked. If no regimes are marked, the certificate type will show as unqualified.
4. Certificate column (R):You must add an explanation if the certificate is qualified and a tax regime is marked with an 'x'. Include as much detail as possible.
5. Unqualified certificate: You can add additional information about your unqualified certificate in the service after uploading the template.
6. Important: Before you upload the template, you must save the template as a CSV (comma delimited) (.csv) file. When saving, choose the option to export the entire workbook to CSV.
7. Important: Do not change the column headings or structure of the template. If you do, it will fail to upload.

Senior Accounting Officer (SAO) is a compliance process impacting the largest customer groups across Large Business (LB) and Mid-Size Business (MSB). Customers are required to submit SAO Certificates and Notifications annually. These are usually received by email/post and LB and MSB operate 2 separate manual compliance processes resulting in laborious and inconsistent responses and application of penalties.
A digital end-to-end solution will enable, automated compliance and data checks, automated penalty flags, ingestion of accurate population data, enhanced exploitation, and analysis capabilities to deliver customer insight, identify risks and deliberate behaviours and facilitate targeted compliance actions upstream; productivity improved by automation.
The SAO process is currently supported with a BDApp within the Large Business area (LB). Currently there is no consistent way of managing this activity across LB & Mid-size Business (MSB).
The current tools / processes HMRC have in operation to manage SAO obligations in Customer Compliance group (CCG) are inconsistent and this means HMRC are not enforcing the legislation fairly and equally across customers.
The existing LB SAO Database Tool provides a limited tactical solution, however it's not fully automated, and its lifespan is short-term. MSB has a limited proactive, partly reactive approach for managing the regime both of which heavily rely on customers disclosing their SAO status. LB and MSB are both impacted.
This affects CCG ability to identify and manage the correct SAO population. HMRC are reliant on the customers to provide data for us to 'see' them. Where HMRC do receive information, it is resource intensive to process/capture it in a useful way.
The request is to digitise the existing SAO process enabling a service that can be used by both LB and MSB.
